hero.headline: US military launches strikes against Iran
hero.body:
The US military launched strikes against multiple targets in Iran on Wednesday evening following a helicopter incident near the Strait of Hormuz, according to US Central Command. The operation began at 5:15 p.m. Eastern time at President Trump's direction after an American Apache helicopter went down off the coast of Oman earlier in the week.

A US official told the Associated Press that the helicopter collided with an Iranian drone, though it remains unclear whether the collision was intentional. Trump initially stated the helicopter had been "shot down" on social media, blaming Iran for the incident. However, in an interview with the Wall Street Journal, Trump downplayed the crash, calling it "wasn't a big deal" and noting that "the pilot is fine." Both crew members were rescued in what the US military described as an unprecedented operation using an unmanned drone boat.

The strikes represent the latest escalation in a cycle of attacks between the two countries. Iran had launched retaliatory strikes on Wednesday morning with missiles and drones targeting facilities in Kuwait, Bahrain, and Jordan. Iran's Revolutionary Guards claimed they had struck the US al-Azraq base in Jordan using long-range missiles and targeted F-35 fighter jet hangars and a command-and-control center. US officials told Reuters that nearly all the missiles and drones launched by Iran were intercepted, with Jordan's armed forces saying they shot down five missiles.

US Central Command characterized the American response as a "proportional response to unjustified Iranian aggression." Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth had warned earlier Wednesday that forthcoming attacks would be strong and clear, indicating the military would conduct operations over multiple nights if needed.

The escalating tensions threaten a fragile ceasefire that the US and Iran announced in April. Iran's foreign minister Abbas Araghchi responded to the American strikes on social media, stating Iran "will leave no attack or threat unanswered" and warned the US to "Leave our region if you want to be safe."

This cycle of strikes follows broader conflict in the Middle East, with Iran and Israel exchanging fire on Monday in what officials described as significant blows to the already strained ceasefire. The ongoing military operations have had global economic consequences, raising energy prices worldwide and making basic goods more expensive.

Despite the military escalation, Trump had expressed optimism about negotiations with Iran just before the helicopter incident. He had said there was "a good chance" of signing a deal within "two or three days," though he provided no details. The president had also suggested that a negotiated settlement would be preferable to extended military campaigns that could cause significant casualties.

cards.headline: Inflation Accelerates to 4.2 Percent as Energy Prices Climb
cards.body:
Consumer prices rose at their fastest pace in three years, reaching 4.2 percent annually in May as energy costs surged following the onset of conflict between the United States and Iran. The acceleration marks the third consecutive monthly increase since the war began and has outpaced wage growth, squeezing household budgets across the country.

Energy prices have climbed sharply as oil markets react to the military operations. The closure of the Strait of Hormuz has disrupted global oil supplies and pushed crude prices higher. These increases have rippled through the economy, affecting transportation costs, heating bills, and the price of goods that depend on fuel for production and distribution. Before the conflict began, inflation stood at 2.4 percent.

Companies face mounting pressure from rising input costs but appear reluctant to pass those increases directly to consumers. Many businesses worry that shoppers, already stretched by months of elevated prices, will reduce spending if prices climb further. Wages have not kept pace with inflation, leaving workers with less purchasing power than they had earlier in the year.

President Trump responded to the inflation figures with an unusual statement, saying "I love the inflation" and expressing no concern about the rising prices due to recent developments in the conflict. His comments represent a significant departure from typical political responses to inflation, which usually emphasize efforts to lower prices. A Trump administration spokesperson stated that the president is focused on the domestic economic situation and is working to bring down prices and reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

The inflation data sent stock markets lower, with major indexes falling more than one percent. Oil prices surged following Trump's remarks about Iran and the ongoing military strikes. Investors now watch to see whether the Federal Reserve will adjust its monetary policy in response to the accelerating price pressures, and whether consumers will reduce spending as their paychecks stretch less far.

The inflation surge extends beyond the United States. Across the eurozone, inflation soared to 3 percent in April as the Iran war drove up energy prices. Energy costs rose 10.9 percent year on year across the euro area, up from 5.1 percent the previous month. The increase pushed eurozone inflation further above the European Central Bank's 2 percent target. Economic growth across the eurozone slowed to just 0.1 percent in the first quarter, down from 0.2 percent previously. Germany outperformed expectations with 0.3 percent growth, while France recorded no growth, with foreign trade making a negative contribution to economic output and household consumption falling.

cards.headline: Oil Prices Rise on Iran Strikes and Energy Market Disruption
cards.teaser: Energy markets reacted to military operations in the Middle East and threats to Iranian oil production.
cards.body:
Oil prices rose following new U.S. airstrikes in the Middle East as tensions escalated between the United States and Iran. U.S. Central Command said the strikes were responding to "unwarranted and continued aggression" from Iran. The military operations disrupted a two-month cease-fire between the two countries.

The attacks marked the latest shock to energy markets already strained by regional conflict. Energy traders are monitoring the situation as the U.S. and Iran continue exchanging strikes, with concerns about potential supply disruptions in a volatile geopolitical environment.

cards.headline: Stock Markets Fall More Than One Percent on Iran Conflict and Inflation Data
cards.teaser: Major indexes declined as investors reacted to rising inflation and renewed military strikes in the Middle East.
cards.body:
The Dow Jones Industrial Average, S&P 500, and Nasdaq each declined more than one percent following the release of inflation data showing a rise to 4.2 percent and U.S. airstrikes against Iran. Technology stocks led the losses while oil-related shares gained as crude prices climbed.

U.S. Central Command said the latest airstrikes responded to what it characterized as "unwarranted and continued aggression" from Iran. The strikes disrupted a two-month cease-fire between the nations and added further volatility to energy markets already sensitive to geopolitical tensions.

cards.headline: US military conducts second day of strikes on Iran
cards.teaser: American forces struck multiple targets in Iran as military operations entered a second day, with President Trump warning Tehran would face consequences for stalled negotiations.
cards.body:
The US military conducted airstrikes on multiple Iranian targets for the second consecutive day. US Central Command said the strikes were in response to what it characterized as "unwarranted and continued aggression" from Iran.

President Trump stated that Tehran would "pay the price" for the stalled negotiations. The escalating military operations pose a threat to diplomatic efforts aimed at ending the conflict between the two countries.

cards.headline: Defense Secretary warns of strong strikes against Iran
cards.teaser: Pete Hegseth said the US military would launch operations Wednesday night and Thursday night if needed.
cards.body:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth warned Wednesday that the U.S. military would conduct strikes against Iran that evening and potentially Thursday night. His statement came hours after President Trump announced plans for additional attacks following retaliatory strikes on Tuesday.

The U.S. Central Command confirmed strikes began at 5:15 p.m. Eastern time at Trump's direction, targeting multiple locations in Iran. The military described the operations as self-defensive responses to what it called "unwarranted and continued aggression" from Iran.

cards.headline: Trump says he welcomes inflation amid Iran military operations
cards.teaser: President Trump stated he embraces rising inflation because the United States is targeting Iranian oil production during ongoing military strikes.
cards.body:
President Trump stated "I love the inflation" after new data showed inflation jumped to 4.2% annually in May, marking a three-year high and the third consecutive monthly increase since the Iran war began. Before the conflict, inflation stood at 2.4%. Speaking from the White House, Trump said he was unconcerned about the price increases due to recent developments in the conflict.

Gas prices have surged amid the military operations, with the national average reaching approximately $4.16 per gallon—about $1 more expensive than the same time last year. The closure of the Strait of Hormuz has affected energy prices. Trump claimed US fuel prices are "not very high, relatively speaking" despite the significant increases Americans are experiencing.

hero.headline: Anti-Immigrant Riots Spread in Northern Ireland After Belfast Stabbing
hero.teaser: Violence erupted across Belfast following a stabbing attack, with cars and a bus set on fire and families driven from their homes.
hero.body:
A stabbing attack in Belfast sparked anti-immigrant violence across the city. A Sudanese man was arrested and charged with attempted murder following the street stabbing on Monday. The unrest escalated as cars and a bus were set on fire, and families were forced to flee their homes.

U.K. leaders urged calm as protests erupted in response to the incident. The victim's family released a statement discouraging people from using the tragedy to fuel violence and hateful actions.

cards.headline: Trump Says U.S. Not Looking to Renew Canada-Mexico Trade Deal
cards.teaser: The president's comments come as the three countries are in talks over renewing their free-trade agreement.
cards.body:
President Trump says the United States is not looking to renew the free-trade agreement with Canada and Mexico. His comments come during a critical phase of negotiations among the three countries over the pact's future.

The existing deal governs billions of dollars in annual commerce between the three nations. Trump's position could reshape North American trade policy and potentially lead to the agreement's expiration or force a complete renegotiation.

cards.headline: At Least 12 Killed in Mass Shooting in Johannesburg
cards.teaser: Multiple attackers stormed a community of tin shacks in South Africa's largest city.
cards.body:
At least 12 people were killed after more than 10 attackers stormed a community of tin shacks in Johannesburg. South African police said they were searching for the suspects following the mass shooting. Investigators were still working to determine the motive behind the attack.

The shooting represents one of the deadliest incidents of violence in Johannesburg in recent months. Police have launched a manhunt for the attackers, who fled the scene after the shooting. The targeted community consists of informal housing structures in one of South Africa's most populous urban areas.

cards.headline: Canada Moves to Ban Social Media for Youth Under 16
cards.teaser: The measure follows a previous failed attempt to get tech companies to protect young users.
cards.body:
Canada is advancing legislation to ban social media use for people under 16 years old. The proposal follows an earlier effort to encourage tech companies to better protect young users, which faced significant backlash from civil liberties advocates concerned about privacy and government overreach.

The age-based ban would make Canada among the world's most restrictive countries on youth social media access. Rather than relying on industry self-regulation, officials have shifted toward a direct legal prohibition.

cards.headline: Pope Blesses Sagrada Familia During Spain Visit
cards.teaser: Pope Leo XIV celebrated Mass at the iconic Barcelona basilica, though the church's completion could displace nearby residents.
cards.body:
Pope Leo XIV blessed the central Tower of Jesus Christ at Barcelona's Sagrada Família, marking a major milestone in the basilica's 144-year construction. The recently completed tower, the tallest of 18 in the temple, brings the structure to its full height of 172.5 metres, making it both the world's tallest church and Barcelona's tallest building. The pontiff celebrated Mass in the presence of Spanish royalty, the prime minister, and hundreds of bishops.

The Pope praised Antoni Gaudí's iconic design as a masterpiece of "stones, colours and light." The basilica was previously consecrated in 2010 by Pope Benedict XVI. Fireworks illuminated the building during the papal visit to Spain.

cards.headline: French Singer Patrick Bruel Faces Rape Investigation
cards.teaser: The performer has been placed under judicial investigation over the allegations.
cards.body:
French singer and actor Patrick Bruel, 67, has been placed under judicial investigation following rape allegations. He was taken into police custody as two new complaints were filed against him. An examining magistrate will conduct a deeper investigation to determine whether to proceed with prosecution.

Bruel is a major figure in French pop culture with multiple top-selling albums and more than 40 film appearances. According to the prosecutor's office in Nanterre, he is being questioned regarding allegations involving 13 victims. Bruel denies the claims.

cards.headline: Pope Leo XIV Visits Barcelona's Sagrada Familia
cards.teaser: The pontiff blessed Gaudi's architectural masterpiece during his trip to Spain.
cards.body:
Pope Leo XIV visited Barcelona's Sagrada Família to bless the completion of its central Jesus Christ tower, the tallest of 18 planned for the basilica. The basilica, designed by Antoni Gaudí, has reached its full height of 172.5 metres after 144 years of construction. It is now both the world's tallest church and Barcelona's tallest building. The pope described the structure as a masterpiece of "stones, colours and light" during the ceremony, which was attended by Spanish royal family members, the prime minister, and hundreds of bishops.

The basilica was previously consecrated by Pope Benedict XVI in 2010. Gaudí's ambitious architectural design has drawn both admiration and criticism over the decades, with questions arising about how closely the completed structure resembles the architect's original vision.

hero.headline: Federal judge blocks Alabama nitrogen gas execution, rules method unconstitutional
hero.body:
A federal judge has permanently blocked Alabama from executing Jeffery Lee using nitrogen gas, determining that the execution method violates the constitutional prohibition against cruel and unusual punishment. The ruling prevents the state from carrying out Lee's scheduled execution on Thursday at an Alabama prison.

Judge Emily C Marks issued the 26-page decision after the 11th Circuit Court of Appeals had reversed her earlier ruling in May that allowed nitrogen gas executions to proceed. In that first decision, Marks had cited testimony from three medical experts stating that "air hunger" caused by nitrogen gas did not constitute an unconstitutional level of pain. However, the appeals court panel disagreed, writing that Alabama's nitrogen hypoxia protocol presented a "substantial risk of serious harm" involving severe pain beyond what is necessary to carry out a death sentence.

Alabama became the first state to use nitrogen gas as an execution method in January 2024, but the practice has faced repeated legal challenges. The method involves placing a mask over the condemned person's face and replacing breathable air with pure nitrogen, causing death by oxygen deprivation.

In her latest ruling, Marks wrote that the constitution does not guarantee a painless death and that litigation will likely accompany any execution method the state pursues. She stated that Lee was not entitled to an injunction preventing execution through lethal injection or the electric chair, the two other authorized execution methods in Alabama. She noted that were Alabama to adopt firing squad, that method would also likely face constitutional challenges.

The case highlights concerns about Lee's sentencing. In 2000, a jury voted to sentence Lee to life without parole for his 1998 murders of Jimmy Ellis and Elaine Thompson. However, a judge overrode the jury's recommendation and sentenced him to death instead. Alabama banned judicial override in 2017 under Governor Kay Ivey, but the law applied only to future cases, not past cases like Lee's. His legal team has requested that Ivey grant clemency and apply the ban retroactively.

Concerns about nitrogen gas executions intensified after the first such execution in the United States. Kenneth Eugene Smith's execution by nitrogen took 22 minutes in 2024. Journalist Lee Hedgepeth, who witnessed the execution, told the BBC: "I've been to four previous executions and I've never seen a condemned inmate thrash in the way that Kenneth Smith reacted to the nitrogen gas."

A spokesman for Alabama's Attorney General Steve Marshall said the state is appealing Marks's decision. The case is likely to reach the United States Supreme Court, which has previously allowed nitrogen executions to proceed.

cards.headline: Eight charged with conspiracy in intimidation campaign targeting University of Michigan officials
cards.teaser: Federal prosecutors indicted eight pro-Palestinian activists for allegedly orchestrating threats and vandalism against University of Michigan regents and Jewish organizations.
cards.body:
Federal prosecutors have charged eight pro-Palestinian activists with conspiracy in connection with an intimidation campaign against University of Michigan officials. The indictment alleges the group orchestrated threats and vandalism aimed at pressuring the school to cut financial ties with Israel.

The charges also include allegations of vandalism targeting companies operating in Michigan and the Jewish Federation of Metropolitan Detroit. The indictment was unsealed Wednesday following FBI operations in the area.

cards.headline: Judge rejects bid to block Trump administration anti-weaponization fund
cards.teaser: A federal judge declined to halt a $1.8 billion Justice Department fund that administration officials say has already been discontinued.
cards.body:
A judge denied a watchdog group's request to block the Trump administration's Anti-Weaponization Fund, a $1.8 billion Justice Department initiative. Administration officials told the court the fund has already been halted, though the watchdog group expressed skepticism about those assurances.

The judge warned the Justice Department while declining to take immediate action. The fund had drawn scrutiny over its stated purpose and scale, prompting the legal challenge from oversight organizations concerned about its implementation and continuation.

cards.headline: Karmelo Anthony sentenced to 35 years for fatal track meet stabbing
cards.teaser: A Texas court sentenced Karmelo Anthony to 35 years in prison for the murder of Austin Metcalf at a Frisco track meet, with the defendant planning to appeal.
cards.body:
Karmelo Anthony received a 35-year prison sentence for the murder of Austin Metcalf, who was stabbed at a Frisco track meet. Anthony's legal team announced plans to appeal the conviction in a case that has drawn national attention and become a focal point of racial debate in Texas.

The trial proceeded under a judge known for maintaining strict courtroom procedures to ensure the proceedings remained legally sound. The case attracted commentary from public figures and sparked discussion about race and justice in the state's legal system.

cards.headline: Trump says he welcomes inflation amid Iran military operations
cards.teaser: President Trump stated he embraces rising inflation because the United States is targeting Iranian oil production during ongoing military strikes.
cards.body:
President Trump stated "I love the inflation" after new data showed inflation jumped to 4.2% annually in May, marking a three-year high and the third consecutive monthly increase since the Iran war began. Before the conflict, inflation stood at 2.4%. Speaking from the White House, Trump said he was unconcerned about the price increases due to recent developments in the conflict.

Gas prices have surged amid the military operations, with the national average reaching approximately $4.16 per gallon—about $1 more expensive than the same time last year. The closure of the Strait of Hormuz has affected energy prices. Trump claimed US fuel prices are "not very high, relatively speaking" despite the significant increases Americans are experiencing.

cards.headline: Somali World Cup referee barred from US entry, welcomed home as hero
cards.teaser: Referee Omar Artan returned to Somalia to a hero's reception after being denied entry to the United States for the World Cup.
cards.body:
Somali referee Omar Artan was selected to officiate matches at the World Cup in the United States, but US authorities denied him entry to the country. The decision prevented him from participating in the tournament and fulfilling what many saw as a career milestone.

Upon returning home, Artan received a hero's welcome in Somalia. Despite being unable to take part in the international event, he was greeted with public support and recognition from his country.

cards.headline: Democrats accept Platner as Senate nominee despite reservations
cards.teaser: Graham Platner won the Maine Democratic Senate primary to face Susan Collins, though some Senate Democrats have not committed to supporting him.
cards.body:
Graham Platner won the Democratic primary in Maine on Tuesday to challenge Republican Senator Susan Collins. Following his victory, progressives rallied around the nominee as he prepared for the general election matchup.

The primary results across four states—Maine, Nevada, North Dakota and South Carolina—offered mixed signals about the direction of both major parties heading into November's midterms. Republicans have already begun using Platner's candidacy in their campaign messaging against Democrats.

cards.headline: AI Companies Raise Cash at Fastest Pace in Decades
cards.teaser: Firms including SpaceX and Alphabet are borrowing and raising equity to fund artificial intelligence development.
cards.body:
Companies competing in the artificial intelligence sector are securing financing at a rate not seen in decades. SpaceX, Alphabet, and other technology firms have accelerated both debt issuance and equity raises to fund their AI operations and infrastructure.

The wave of capital raising reflects the enormous costs associated with developing and deploying AI systems, which require massive data centers and computing power. Investors have shown willingness to provide funding despite concerns about when these investments will generate returns.

cards.headline: Oracle Reports Higher Profit on Cloud Revenue Growth
cards.teaser: The software company posted earnings that exceeded expectations, driven by its cloud computing business.
cards.body:
Oracle reported quarterly results that beat analyst forecasts, with profits rising on surging revenue from its cloud computing operations. The company has been rapidly transforming its business to focus on cloud services and artificial intelligence infrastructure.

Despite the positive earnings, Oracle's stock declined following the announcement. The company revealed plans to raise an additional 20 billion dollars to fund data center construction and expansion, which some investors viewed as a significant capital commitment during uncertain market conditions.

cards.headline: SpaceX IPO Expected to Create 4,400 Employee Millionaires
cards.teaser: The rocket company's planned market debut would generate substantial wealth for current and former workers.
cards.body:
SpaceX's anticipated initial public offering is projected to turn approximately 4,400 current and former employees into millionaires through their stock holdings. The company, led by Elon Musk, has provided equity compensation to workers over the years as it has grown into one of the most valuable private companies.

The market debut would represent one of the largest technology IPOs in recent years. While Musk's own stake could push his net worth toward a trillion dollars, the offering would also distribute significant wealth among the broader employee base that has built the company's rocket and satellite businesses.

cards.headline: Frasers Group Offers 1.73 Billion Pounds for Hugo Boss
cards.teaser: The retail group controlled by Mike Ashley has bid to acquire the remaining shares of the German fashion brand.
cards.body:
Mike Ashley's Frasers Group has tabled a £1.73 billion bid to acquire the remaining shares of Hugo Boss that it does not currently own. The retail company already holds just over a quarter of the German fashion brand.

The offer would give Frasers complete ownership of Hugo Boss and allow it to fully integrate the brand into its broader retail operations.

hero.headline: Hackers claim breach of Oracle PeopleSoft servers at over 100 organizations
hero.body:
The ShinyHunters hacking gang claims to have compromised the Oracle PeopleSoft servers of more than 100 organizations, including many universities. The alleged breach represents a significant security incident affecting enterprise resource planning systems used by institutions across multiple sectors.

Oracle PeopleSoft is a widely deployed enterprise software platform that organizations use to manage human resources, financial operations, and student administration systems. Universities have adopted the platform extensively for managing enrollment, payroll, and academic records. The claimed compromise raises concerns about potential exposure of sensitive institutional and personal data stored within these systems.

ShinyHunters has previously claimed responsibility for data breaches targeting major companies and institutions. The group has a history of selling stolen databases and credentials on underground forums. The gang's latest claim suggests a coordinated campaign targeting organizations running PeopleSoft infrastructure, though the full scope of any data exfiltration has not been independently verified.

The security implications for affected organizations could be substantial. PeopleSoft systems typically contain employee records, student information, financial data, and authentication credentials. Universities may need to assess whether sensitive information was accessed and notify affected individuals if personal data was compromised. Organizations running PeopleSoft will need to review their server configurations and security protocols to determine vulnerability.

Oracle has not publicly commented on the alleged breach. Universities and other organizations using PeopleSoft will likely conduct internal security audits and may implement additional protective measures while investigating whether their systems were affected. The incident highlights ongoing cybersecurity challenges facing institutions that rely on enterprise software platforms to manage critical operations and sensitive data.

cards.headline: Former xAI engineer sues over firing after raising Grok safety concerns
cards.teaser: A lawsuit alleges the engineer was terminated for flagging AI safety issues with Grok shortly before SpaceX's initial public offering.
cards.body:
A former xAI engineer has sued the company and SpaceX, claiming he was terminated for raising safety concerns about Grok, the company's AI chatbot. The firing allegedly happened shortly before SpaceX's initial public offering.

The lawsuit alleges retaliation for the engineer's internal reporting of safety issues related to Grok's development and deployment.

cards.headline: Scientists discover 5.3 million-year-old whale graveyard in Indian Ocean
cards.teaser: Researchers found a deep-sea necropolis in the Diamantina Zone stretching hundreds of miles across the ocean floor.
cards.body:
The oldest and most extensive whale graveyard ever documented has been found in the south-eastern Indian Ocean's Diamantina fracture zone. Fossils at the site date back more than 5 million years, and the necropolis stretches hundreds of miles across the sea floor at depths exceeding 7 kilometres—far deeper than the typical whale falls found at less than 4 kilometres.

The discovery reveals species and ecosystems previously unknown to science. Dead whales sinking to the ocean floor, known as whale falls, create rich environments that support diverse marine life. This unprecedented site expands our understanding of deep-sea ecosystems and ancient whale populations.

cards.headline: Amazon borrows $17.5 billion from banks to fund AI spending
cards.teaser: The loan follows a recent bond sale as the company continues significant investments in artificial intelligence infrastructure.
cards.body: Amazon secured a $17.5 billion bank loan to support its artificial intelligence spending, adding to recent capital raises. The borrowing highlights how technology companies are rapidly accumulating debt as they compete in the AI arms race, spending heavily to keep pace with rivals in developing and deploying AI infrastructure and capabilities.

cards.headline: Apple announces over 250 new features across iOS 27 and macOS Golden Gate
cards.teaser: The company released a comprehensive list of changes coming to its operating systems this fall.
cards.body:
Apple published details of more than 250 features and improvements planned for iOS 27, macOS Golden Gate, and other operating systems launching this fall. The updates span multiple device categories and services across the Apple ecosystem.

New features include significant upgrades to Apple Maps in iOS 27, including enhanced tree visualization and a new Local Lists feature. The company also unveiled various intelligence experiences and service improvements designed to enhance functionality across its hardware lineup.

cards.headline: Google Gemini app experiences partial outage affecting some users
cards.teaser: Google acknowledged service disruptions with users reporting error codes 1099 and 1076.
cards.body:
Google's Gemini artificial intelligence app experienced a partial outage affecting a portion of its user base. The company acknowledged the service disruption after users reported receiving error messages indicating something went wrong with the platform.

Google stated that the majority of users should now be able to access the service following recovery efforts. Users had reported specific error codes including 1099 and 1076 during the outage period. The company has not disclosed the cause of the disruption or the total number of affected users.

cards.headline: Apple and Google add support for Thread 1.4 protocol
cards.teaser: Both companies have integrated the updated smart home connectivity standard into their platforms.
cards.body:
Apple and Google are updating their smart home streaming devices to support Thread 1.4, the latest version of the connectivity protocol. The update has arrived on compatible Apple TVs through the tvOS 27 developer beta and on the Google TV Streamer via a software update.

Thread 1.4 enables improved communication and interoperability between smart home devices by providing low-power wireless networking. These streaming devices now serve as better hubs for managing connected smart home ecosystems.

hero.headline: Patrick Mahomes Signs Record NFL Contract Extension Worth Over $500 Million
hero.body:
Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes has agreed to a restructured contract that makes him the highest-paid player in NFL history. The reworked deal is valued at $504.75 million, with incentives and escalators potentially pushing the total beyond $520 million.

Mahomes originally signed a 10-year, $450 million contract with the Chiefs in 2020, which was groundbreaking at the time. The new extension adds two additional years to that agreement, keeping him with Kansas City through the 2033 season when he will be 38 years old.

The deal surpasses the previous record held by Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott. Mahomes becomes the first NFL player to secure a contract exceeding half a billion dollars in total value, cementing his status as the league's most valuable asset at the quarterback position.

Since becoming the Chiefs' starting quarterback in 2018, Mahomes has established himself as one of the most accomplished players in professional football. A two-time NFL MVP, he has led Kansas City to multiple Super Bowl appearances and championships. His combination of on-field excellence and marketability has made him one of the most valuable athletes in sports.

The restructured agreement reflects the rapidly escalating compensation for elite quarterbacks in the modern NFL. Team owners and general managers continue to allocate unprecedented resources to franchise quarterbacks, recognizing them as essential to sustained competitive success. Mahomes' contract extension is likely to influence future negotiations for other top-tier players at the position.

The Chiefs organization has made it a priority to retain Mahomes for the remainder of his career. The restructured deal allows the team to address salary cap considerations while ensuring their star player receives the highest compensation in the sport. The agreement includes various incentives and escalators that could increase the total value depending on performance and other factors.

Mahomes' extended contract demonstrates the Chiefs' commitment to building around their core player. His presence has transformed the franchise into one of the NFL's most successful organizations in recent years. The quarterback's leadership and consistent performance have made him invaluable to the team's championship aspirations.

The contract negotiations had been anticipated by league observers, as Mahomes' original deal was set to expire after the 2031 season. The extension provides clarity for both the player and the organization regarding their long-term partnership. Financial details about guaranteed money and the specific structure of the contract have been reported by multiple sources covering the negotiations.

With this deal, Mahomes has solidified his place among the NFL's elite players and secured his financial future while remaining committed to winning championships with the Chiefs.

cards.headline: American Teen Cooper Lutkenhaus Upsets Olympic Champion Emmanuel Wanyonyi in Oslo 800m
cards.teaser: 17-year-old American Cooper Lutkenhaus defeated Olympic champion Emmanuel Wanyonyi in the men's 800 meters at the Diamond League meeting in Oslo.
cards.body:
American Cooper Lutkenhaus, 17, delivered a remarkable performance at the Diamond League meet in Oslo, defeating Olympic 800-meter champion Emmanuel Wanyonyi by just 0.01 seconds. The victory adds another impressive achievement to the teenager's growing track record at the Bislett Stadion, one of track and field's most storied venues.

The same competition proved more challenging for fellow teenager Gout Gout, the Australian sprinter, who finished sixth in the 200 meters. The result underscored the heightened level of competition at elite Diamond League events.

cards.headline: Formula 1 Agrees to Two-Step Engine Design Change After Criticism
cards.teaser: Formula 1 has agreed to modify engine design in response to criticism of this year's new technical regulations.
cards.body:
Formula 1 has approved a two-step plan to modify engine design following criticism of this year's new rules. The phased approach will allow teams time to implement the changes across multiple stages.

The decision comes in response to feedback from the racing community regarding the current technical regulations. By breaking the modifications into steps rather than implementing them all at once, teams will have greater flexibility in adapting to the revised engine specifications.

cards.headline: Joe Root Named Interim England Test Captain, Replacing Ben Stokes
cards.teaser: England has turned to Joe Root to serve as interim Test captain in place of Ben Stokes.
cards.body:
England's cricket team has appointed Joe Root as interim Test captain following Ben Stokes' absence from the squad. Stokes will miss England's second Test against New Zealand at The Oval after an incident in a London nightclub.

Root, who previously captained England's Test team before Stokes took over, returns to the role to provide leadership continuity during this transition. The ECB's decision reflects confidence in Root's experience and proven captaincy credentials from his earlier tenure.

cards.headline: Madison Square Garden Disputes NYC Security Measures Ahead of Knicks Game 4
cards.teaser: MSG continues its disagreement with New York City officials over watch party arrangements hours before the Knicks' NBA Finals Game 4.
cards.body:
Madison Square Garden owner James Dolan's company has criticized New York City officials over security measures for the Knicks' NBA Finals Game 4. The dispute involves Mayor Zohran Mamdani and Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch, whom MSG Sports called "party poopers" in media statements.

The enhanced security strategy includes a large restricted zone and additional access controls around the arena. These measures followed disorder at a Game 3 watch party in Bryant Park on Monday, where arrests were made, property was damaged, and police officers were assaulted. The NYPD has banned spontaneous gatherings outside Madison Square Garden ahead of the game.

cards.headline: Texas Tech Threatens Legal Action Over Potential Big 12 Sanctions for Brendan Sorsby
cards.teaser: Texas Tech will file a lawsuit if the Big 12 Conference attempts to impose sanctions related to quarterback Brendan Sorsby.
cards.body:
Texas Tech University has indicated it will take legal action against the Big 12 Conference if the league moves forward with sanctions related to quarterback Brendan Sorsby. The warning came after Big 12 athletic directors held a conference call to discuss the situation and air grievances over a recent ruling involving Sorsby.

Texas Tech officials defended Sorsby amid a controversy involving gambling addiction. The university's stance has created tension within the conference, with one Texas Tech representative stating the school is prepared to go to battle over potential sanctions. A Texas judge's ruling in the case has drawn criticism, with some commentators calling it the biggest scandal in college sports.

cards.headline: New Jersey Prepares Transportation Plan for World Cup at MetLife Stadium
cards.teaser: New Jersey is ramping up transit services and implementing special transportation rules for World Cup matches at MetLife Stadium.
cards.body:
New Jersey officials are ramping up transportation infrastructure ahead of the World Cup at MetLife Stadium, which will host the tournament opener. NJ Transit is increasing service and staffing levels to manage the influx of fans traveling to the venue.

Authorities have restricted drop-off access at the stadium during World Cup games to Uber only. Transportation planners are preparing for potential disruptions to Amtrak service and developing contingency plans to move large crowds to and from MetLife Stadium.

hero.headline: Third Jump Street Film in Development With Original Stars
hero.body:
A third installment in the Jump Street franchise is moving forward, with Jonah Hill, Channing Tatum and Ice Cube in talks to reprise their roles. The film, titled 24 Jump Street, will continue the R-rated crime comedy series that launched in 2012.

Rodney Rothman, known for his work on Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse, will direct the project. Rothman co-wrote the script with Hill and Meghan Malloy. Returning producers Phil Lord and Christopher Miller, who helmed the first two films, are also involved with the production.

The original 21 Jump Street arrived in 2012 as a comedic adaptation of the 1980s television series, following two young officers who go undercover at a high school. The film earned over 201 million dollars worldwide. The sequel, 22 Jump Street, came out in 2014 and grossed more than 331 million dollars globally, relocating the story to a college campus.

Hill and Tatum played Schmidt and Jenko, a pair of mismatched police partners, in both previous films. Ice Cube appeared as Captain Dickson, their superior officer. The franchise gained recognition for combining action with self-aware humor that frequently commented on sequel conventions and franchise expansion.

While negotiations with the three lead actors continue, no release date has been set for 24 Jump Street. The franchise experienced an extended development period following the second film's release, with several concepts considered over the years. One notable idea involved a crossover with the Men in Black series, though that project never moved forward. The second film concluded with comedic references to potential future sequels and multiple numbered installments.

This announcement marks the first significant development on a third Jump Street film in years. The franchise established itself as a successful property during the 2010s, appealing to audiences who enjoyed the blend of comedy and action. The creative team behind the previous films demonstrated skill at balancing humor with franchise commentary, making the third installment a potentially significant project for the studio.

The involvement of returning filmmakers and the willingness of the original cast to return suggest confidence in the material. Rothman's recent success with Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse indicates he brings experience with large-scale productions and visual storytelling. His collaboration with Hill on the script suggests the actors maintain creative input on their characters and the story direction.

The Jump Street series has proven its commercial viability, with each installment performing well at the global box office. Whether 24 Jump Street can match or exceed the financial success of its predecessors will depend on several factors, including the script's quality, the chemistry between returning cast members, and audience appetite for another installment. The franchise's success with self-aware humor about sequels may provide fresh material for exploring what a third film means for the series moving forward.

cards.headline: Xbox CEO Warns of Business Challenges in Staff Memo
cards.teaser: New Xbox chief executive Asha Sharma told employees the gaming division faces significant operational difficulties.
cards.body:
Xbox CEO Asha Sharma outlined significant challenges facing the Microsoft-owned gaming business in a memo to staff. The note addressed what Sharma described as "surprising and even frustrating" realities and discussed reshaping the company's operations.

According to sources familiar with Microsoft's plans, the Xbox division will undergo significant layoffs next month. The cuts could potentially include studio closures. Sharma had previously hinted at "making hard choices" as the company prepares for the organizational changes ahead.

cards.headline: House of the Dragon Season 3 Premieres at Taormina Film Festival
cards.teaser: The Italian festival screened the first episode of the HBO series in a Greek theater dating to the third century B.C.
cards.body:
Italy's Taormina Film Festival opened with a screening of the first episode of House of the Dragon Season 3. The event took place in the Sicilian resort's Greek theater, which dates back to the third century B.C., with 5,000 spectators attending.

The screening used a large outdoor screen to show the HBO series premiere. The Taormina festival regularly uses the ancient venue for major film and television events. House of the Dragon is the prequel series to Game of Thrones, focusing on the Targaryen civil war known as the Dance of the Dragons.

cards.headline: Billie Jean King Documentary to Open Croatia Film Festival
cards.teaser: The ESPN 30 for 30 film directed by Liz Garbus will screen at the third annual festival in Sibenik.
cards.body:
"Give Me The Ball!" will premiere as the opening film of the third annual Croatia International Film Festival on July 24 in the coastal city of Sibenik. Directed by Oscar-nominated filmmaker Liz Garbus and Elizabeth Wolff, the documentary is part of ESPN's acclaimed 30 for 30 series.

The film chronicles the life and legacy of tennis legend Billie Jean King, who won 39 Grand Slam titles and became a pioneering advocate for gender equality in sports.

cards.headline: Billy Preston Documentary First Film Available for Oscar Voters
cards.teaser: Paris Barclay's film about the musician became the first entry uploaded to the Academy Screening Room for the 99th Academy Awards.
cards.body:
Paris Barclay's documentary "Billy Preston: That's the Way God Planned It" has become the first film uploaded to the Academy Screening Room for the 99th Academy Awards. The members-only platform allows Oscar voters to stream eligible films across various award categories.

The upload marks the unofficial beginning of awards season. Preston was a keyboardist and singer who collaborated with the Beatles and other prominent artists throughout his career.

cards.headline: Tyla to Voice Character in Toy Story 5
cards.teaser: The South African pop star will play an inflatable flamingo in a sub-Saharan edition of the animated film.
cards.body:
Tyla will make her voice acting debut in the sub-Saharan edition of Toy Story 5. The South African pop star will play an inflatable flamingo character in the fifth installment of the animated franchise.

Tyla described herself as a Toy Story fanatic. Disney and Pixar produce localized versions of their films for different regions, with variations in voice casting and cultural references. Toy Story 5 continues the series that began in 1995.

cards.headline: Upworthy Names Amanda Farrand as Chief Executive
cards.teaser: The digital publisher hired the former Imagine Entertainment and Hello Sunshine executive to lead the company.
cards.body:
Amanda Farrand joined Upworthy as chief executive on May 26. The Los Angeles-based company operates as a digital aggregator and producer of viral uplifting content. Farrand previously held senior positions at Imagine Entertainment and Hello Sunshine.

Upworthy focuses on feel-good stories and positive content distributed across digital platforms. Farrand's background includes work in entertainment production and media strategy. The company aims to generate revenue while maintaining its mission of sharing optimistic stories.

hero.headline: US military launches strikes against Iran
hero.body:
The US military launched strikes against multiple targets in Iran on Wednesday evening following a helicopter incident near the Strait of Hormuz, according to US Central Command. The operation began at 5:15 p.m. Eastern time at President Trump's direction after an American Apache helicopter went down off the coast of Oman earlier in the week.

A US official told the Associated Press that the helicopter collided with an Iranian drone, though it remains unclear whether the collision was intentional. Trump initially stated the helicopter had been "shot down" on social media, blaming Iran for the incident. However, in an interview with the Wall Street Journal, Trump downplayed the crash, calling it "wasn't a big deal" and noting that "the pilot is fine." Both crew members were rescued in what the US military described as an unprecedented operation using an unmanned drone boat.

The strikes represent the latest escalation in a cycle of attacks between the two countries. Iran had launched retaliatory strikes on Wednesday morning with missiles and drones targeting facilities in Kuwait, Bahrain, and Jordan. Iran's Revolutionary Guards claimed they had struck the US al-Azraq base in Jordan using long-range missiles and targeted F-35 fighter jet hangars and a command-and-control center. US officials told Reuters that nearly all the missiles and drones launched by Iran were intercepted, with Jordan's armed forces saying they shot down five missiles.

US Central Command characterized the American response as a "proportional response to unjustified Iranian aggression." Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth had warned earlier Wednesday that forthcoming attacks would be strong and clear, indicating the military would conduct operations over multiple nights if needed.

The escalating tensions threaten a fragile ceasefire that the US and Iran announced in April. Iran's foreign minister Abbas Araghchi responded to the American strikes on social media, stating Iran "will leave no attack or threat unanswered" and warned the US to "Leave our region if you want to be safe."

This cycle of strikes follows broader conflict in the Middle East, with Iran and Israel exchanging fire on Monday in what officials described as significant blows to the already strained ceasefire. The ongoing military operations have had global economic consequences, raising energy prices worldwide and making basic goods more expensive.

Despite the military escalation, Trump had expressed optimism about negotiations with Iran just before the helicopter incident. He had said there was "a good chance" of signing a deal within "two or three days," though he provided no details. The president had also suggested that a negotiated settlement would be preferable to extended military campaigns that could cause significant casualties.

cards.headline: Inflation reaches 4.2 percent in May, highest in three years
cards.teaser: New Labor Department figures show inflation rising to its highest level in three years as the Iran conflict drives up consumer costs.
cards.body:
Inflation surged to 4.2 percent in May, marking the highest rate in three years, according to a Labor Department report. The increase represents the third consecutive monthly rise since the U.S. and Israel launched military operations against Iran. Gasoline prices spiked significantly following the conflict, which disrupted energy markets. Inflation stood at 2.4 percent before the war began.

The timing poses challenges for President Trump in an election year focused on affordability. The administration faces pressure over rising energy costs tied to Middle East developments and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz.

cards.headline: House Speaker defends Trump remarks on inflation
cards.teaser: Mike Johnson told reporters Trump's comment about loving inflation was taken out of context.
cards.body:
House Speaker Mike Johnson defended President Trump's statement about loving inflation, telling CNN the remark was totally out of context. The GOP leader said people understood what Trump was talking about when he made the comment.

Trump faced criticism after making the inflation comment to reporters during a period of concern about skyrocketing energy costs resulting from the Iran war. Johnson's defense came as new inflation figures showed prices rising 4.2 percent in May.

cards.headline: Trump undergoes checkup with 22 medical specialists
cards.teaser: The president saw about twice as many specialists as in prior checkups, though the White House declined to identify them.
cards.body:
President Trump was examined by 22 medical specialists during a recent checkup, according to the White House. Past statements indicate Trump saw about a dozen specialists for prior checkups, making this examination significantly more extensive.

The White House declined to identify which specialists assessed the president. The expanded medical team appears to set a new standard for presidential health examinations, though officials did not explain the reason for the increased number of doctors involved.

cards.headline: Wisconsin dairy farmers sue Trump administration over mandatory fees
cards.teaser: Three farmers filed a lawsuit challenging requirements to provide operational data and pay fees to the Dairy Checkoff Program.
cards.body:
Three Wisconsin farmers filed a lawsuit against the Trump administration on Wednesday over mandatory participation in the Dairy Checkoff Program. The suit challenges requirements that dairy producers provide operational data and pay fees to fund promotion and research efforts.

Dairy farmers currently pay 15 cents for every 100 pounds of milk sold toward the checkoff program. Dairy importers pay 7.5 cents per 100 pounds. The lawsuit seeks to end the mandatory nature of these payments and data reporting requirements.

cards.headline: Facebook settlement bonus payments fall short of expectations
cards.teaser: Individual payouts from the $725 million settlement fund proved much smaller than many recipients anticipated.
cards.body:
The BBC Sport article you provided is about a tennis player retiring from a match due to injury. It's not related to the Facebook settlement story.

I'm returning your original card text unchanged:

Bonus payments from the Facebook settlement are being distributed, but recipients report disappointment with the amounts. The individual payouts have proved much smaller than the $725 million total fund suggested to many claimants.

The settlement fund's impressive total size did not translate into large individual payments when divided among all eligible claimants. Many people expressed surprise at how little they received from their share of the settlement.

cards.headline: Tim Tebow backs Hawley anti-exploitation measure in immigration bill
cards.teaser: The former NFL quarterback joined the senator to promote a provision combating child exploitation that became law.
cards.body:
Senator Josh Hawley and former NFL quarterback Tim Tebow championed a child protection provision that was included in an immigration enforcement bill signed into law by President Trump on Wednesday. The legislation, worth nearly $70 billion, fully funds Immigration and Customs Enforcement and Border Patrol through the fiscal year.

Hawley and Tebow highlighted the anti-exploitation measure as a key component of the broader immigration enforcement package.
